  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  JULY 14, 2022

 A special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Himmelrich at 6:08 p.m.,
 on Thursday, July 14, 2022, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

 Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Sue Himmelrich
  Mayor Pro Tem Kristin McCowan
  Councilmember Phil Brock
  Councilmember Gleam Davis
  Councilmember Lana Negrete (arrived at 6:22 p.m.)
  Councilmember Oscar de la Torre
  Councilmember Christine Parra (arrived at 6:20 p.m.)

  Also Present:  City Manager David White
  City Attorney Douglas Sloan
  City Clerk Denise Anderson-Warren

  present except Councilmembers Parra and Negrete. Councilmember Davis led the
  assemblage in the Pledge of Allegiance.

AGENDA  Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem McCowan, to hear
MANAGEMENT  Item 12.A. before the Board and Commission appointments. The motion was
  approved by voice vote, with Councilmembers Parra and Negrete absent.

SECTION 615  adoption of all ordinances and resolutions shall be by reading of title only unless a
  Councilmember present dissents. There were no dissentions from Councilmembers
  present.

ITIEM:

PUBLIC HEARINGS:  12.A. Adoption of Resolution Nos. 11442 (CCS) through 11444 (CCS) and
OCEAN AVENUE  Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance to adopt the Ocean Avenue
PROJECT  Project Development Agreement, was presented.
DEVELOPMENT
AGREEMENT  Recommended Action
  It is recommended that the Council take the following actions:

  1  July 14, 2022
   1. Affirm that the Ocean Avenue Project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  Section 15182 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines;
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 11442 (CCS) certifying the Final Environmental
  Impact Report (EIR) prepared for the project in accordance with CEQA;
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 11443 (CCS) adopting a Statement of Overriding
  Considerations to support approval of the Development Agreement based
  upon the Final EIR and other information provided in the record and adopting
  a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program;
  4. Adopt Resolution No. 11444 (CCS) amending the 1992 Local Coastal
  Program Land Use Plan (LUP) for consistency with the 2010 General Plan
  and 2017 Downtown Community Plan standards for the project site; and
  5. Introduce an ordinance for first reading to adopt Development Agreement
  13DEV-004 for the Ocean Avenue Project.

  Councilmember de la Torre recused himself from this item to avoid any perceived
  conflict of interest, because Mr. Worth’s Family Foundation has supported the Pico
  Youth and Family Center in previous years.

Councilmember de la  Ex-Parti Communication
Torre was excused at
6:18 p.m.  Councilmember Davis, on June 27th met with Jeff Worth at his office on Ocean
  Avenue at 4 p.m. to discuss the project and examine the two models that are here in
  the Council chambers.

Councilmember Parra  Mayor Pro Tem McCowan, on July 8th met with Mr. Worth, Paula Larmore and
arrived at 6:20 p.m.  Jenna for about an hour at the site going over the project and hearing their
  presentation. Additionally, Jenna bought the Mayor Pro Tem a coffee.

Councilmember Negrete Mayor Himmelrich, on July 7th at 3:00 p.m. met with Mr. Worth, Jenna, with Tony
arrived at 6:22 p.m.  Vazquez and looked at the models. Met and talked a long time ago about issues of
  concern that have since been addressed.

  Councilmember Brock, met with Jeff Worth on May 23rd at 1 p.m. to view the
  models.

  Councilmember Parra, on July 8th, met with Mr. Worth, Jenna and Paula Larmore to
  discuss and review the scope of the project.

  Councilmember Negrete, at the end of May or the beginning of June, met with Paula
  Larmore at the project site to discuss about the length of the project and to have
  questions answered.

  Members of the public Alicia Mignano, Emily McCarron, Tommy Faavae, Kurt
  Petersen, Denise Barton, Matt Stauffer, Bruria Finkel, James Mary O’Connor,
  Elizabeth Hartwell, Albin Gielicz, Tom Cleys (time donated by Carolyne Edwards),

  2  July 14, 2022
   Zakiya, Nancy Cetner, Chris Hannan, Christina Sanchez, and Zachary Gaidzik spoke
  to the recommended action.

  Questions asked and answered included: where is the concern about people being
  able to access the rooftop, even if they don’t have a dollar to pay; what happened
  with the ability to allow free entry for those 12 or 13 and under; is there a way to
  make sure that this museum reflects the history and feel of Santa Monica, including
  the Pier, the Historical Society, and the Arts; how did they arrive at 285 parking
  spaces, and is there a way to construct the agreement to say a maximum of 285
  parking spaces; will there be opportunities to change the language to say Santa
  Monica schools, for access, but providing transportation would only be for public
  schools; and, can the days the rooftop is closed for non-profits events goes from five
  to six days.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to: set our
  standards high for the types of art that will be displayed and rotated in the museum;
  amend agreement to so that the museum allow free entry for 10 and under; amend
  agreement to add language to the agreement to say up to a maximum of 285 parking
  spaces; amend agreement to say Santa Monica schools, but transportation will only
  be for Santa Monica public schools, and amend the agreement to change the number
  of days the rooftop will be closed for non-profit events from five to six days; thanks
  to Mr. Gehry for giving back to the city with this project; this project will be a tourist
  magnet with the architecture of the buildings, as well as the museum; gratified by the
  developers attention to detail, being considerate of what Santa Monica wants and
  needs; and, appreciation for the open space connected to the living space.

  The applicant was agreeable to the amendments proposed during discussion.

  Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem McCowan, to approve
  the staff recommendation with the adjustments and amendments discussed. The
  motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Brock, Negrete, Davis, Parra
  Mayor Pro Tem McCowan, Mayor Himmelrich
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmember de la Torre
